prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” HVAC company for every Phoenix homeowner — the right choice depends on your location, budget, the problem (repair vs. replacement), whether you need emergency service, and whether your unit is under warranty. I can narrow options for you if you tell me your zip code and whether this is urgent. Meanwhile, here’s a practical way to find the best contractor and what to ask them.

How to find a reliable HVAC company in Phoenix
- Check reviews on Google and Yelp (look for many recent, detailed reviews about AC repair).
- Verify license and complaints at the Arizona Registrar of Contractors (search ROC license).
- Look for NATE-certified technicians (North American Technician Excellence).
- Check the BBB for ratings and complaint history.
- Ask for proof of insurance (general liability and workers’ comp).
- Get 2–3 written bids to compare diagnosis, parts, labor, and warranties.

Key questions to ask when you call
- Are you licensed with the Arizona ROC? What’s your license number?
- Are your technicians NATE-certified?
- Do you carry insurance? (ask for proof)
- Do you charge a diagnostic/dispatch fee? Is it waived if we hire you?
- What’s included in the written estimate (parts, labor, permits)?
- What warranties do you offer on parts and labor?
- Do you offer emergency/after-hours service and what’s the extra charge?
- Will you provide references from recent local AC repairs?

What to expect (typical ranges and guidance)
- Diagnostic/visit fee: often $75–$150 (sometimes applied to repair cost).
- Common minor repairs (capacitor, contactor, fan motor): $150–$600.
- Refrigerant recharge (if lawful and appropriate): $150–$400 (cost depends on type and amount).
- Major components (compressor, condensing unit) or full system replacement: $1,500–$7,000+ depending on size and efficiency.
- If the unit is older than ~10–15 years or needs major components replaced, replacing the system may be more cost-effective.

Red flags to avoid
- No written estimate or vague scope of work.
- Pressuring you to replace components without showing evidence.
- Very low price compared to others without explanation.
- No ROC license or refusal to provide license/insurance info.

If you want, I can:
- Recommend 3–5 well-reviewed Phoenix-area HVAC companies (if you give your zip code).
- Draft a short phone/script template you can use to call for estimates.
- Help compare 2–3 quotes if you paste them here.

Tell me your zip code and whether this is an emergency and I’ll give tailored recommendations and a call script.
